evidence_claims.claim: North American 120/240 V commonly arises from center-tapped single-phase transformer secondary

supports.location: North and Central American residential distribution paragraph

evidence_claims.limitations: Not every North American building uses that source arrangement.

evidence_claims.claim: Split-phase outer-to-midpoint voltages are opposite phasors, yielding 240 V outer-to-outer
evidence_claims.limitations: Ideal equal secondary assumption; real voltage regulation differs.

evidence_claims.claim: Higher voltage at equal resistive power reduces current in the simplified model
evidence_claims.limitations: Does not determine safe conductor size.

evidence_claims.claim: Balanced split-phase resistive leg loads cause neutral-current cancellation in ideal model
evidence_claims.limitations: Opposite leg phasors and unity-power-factor assumption required.

evidence_claims.claim: Open center-tap neutral with unequal loads can lead to unequal series voltages
evidence_claims.limitations: Fault voltages depend on topology and extra load paths.

evidence_claims.claim: Balanced three-phase sinusoids have phase separation of 120 degrees
evidence_claims.limitations: Three-phase angle model is standard phasor derivation; source specifically not a comprehensive 3-phase text.

evidence_claims.claim: Balanced wye line-to-line voltage magnitude is sqrt(3) times phase-neutral voltage
evidence_claims.limitations: Exactly true for balanced sinusoids; nominal rounding affects labels.

evidence_claims.claim: 230/400 V and 120/208 V are standardized supply families but not global rules
evidence_claims.limitations: Both Schneider sources are same publisher and do not count as independent corroboration.

evidence_claims.claim: Delta connections and wye connections do not necessarily offer same neutral voltages
evidence_claims.limitations: Detailed high-leg identification and application needs local code and equipment specifics.

evidence_claims.claim: At fixed resistance, a 2400 W 240 V heater draws about 1803 W at 208 V

supports.location: Section 9.5 P equals V squared over R

evidence_claims.limitations: Purely resistive fixed-temperature model, not equipment approval.

evidence_claims.claim: Balanced three-phase sinusoidal real power is sqrt(3) V_LL I_L times power factor

supports.location: Section 15.4 AC power and power factor

evidence_claims.limitations: Formula assumes balance and sinusoidal definition of power factor.

evidence_claims.claim: Four-wire three-phase neutral can carry unbalance and triplen harmonic current

supports.location: Influence of harmonics on neutral sizing

evidence_claims.limitations: Device and waveform specifics matter; instrument measurement required for actual values.

evidence_claims.claim: Regional nominal voltage and frequency differ across systems
evidence_claims.limitations: Precise voltage tolerance and frequency require actual utility and national rules.

evidence_claims.claim: Source phasor compatibility matters to 120/240 versus 120/208 equipment
evidence_claims.limitations: Individual appliance allowable voltage is product specific.
